title: RTX 4090 native component v0.6.4-beta.1: two ceiling sessions survive a graceful stop
changes: host-KV pool 4096 -> 11264 MiB so restore can admit the lane's own ceiling-sized sessions
an export is refused when the configuration's pool could not admit the checkpoint back
restore declines name their gate; the startup line publishes host-kv-restorable=<tokens>

measured_on_packaged_bytes.workload: two sessions of about 125,900 input tokens, one alternating continuation each, explicit checkpoints, graceful --stop-event shutdown, restart, resume by planted desk code
measured_on_packaged_bytes.graceful_stop: shutdown: saved 2, nothing to save 0, refused 0

shipped_configuration_it_replaces.single_ceiling_session: explicit checkpoint reported 4,834,325,255 B saved; after a graceful stop and restart the session answered HTTP 404 previous_response_not_found
shipped_configuration_it_replaces.two_ceiling_sessions: 4 of 4 continuations lost; one explicit checkpoint refused 409; stop saved 1 refused 1; both sessions 404 after restart
shipped_configuration_it_replaces.with_the_new_binary_on_that_pool: the export is now refused up front (HTTP 409, 'checkpoint save refused: program refused continuation export') instead of reporting a save that cannot be restored

tests: ninfer_checkpoint_io_contract_test: the restore bound reproduces the lane's disclosed 119,616-token value, clamps at kv_capacity, holds the exact page boundary, and halves under a speculative extent
ninfer_resource_manager_test: every restore decline names its gate, including a forwarded host-KV capacity refusal
both suites pass on Windows/MSVC in this component's own build (6/6 focused targets)
not_yet_done: the component is built and packaged but not published; the product release that carries it, its public-install acceptance, and the RTX 5090 image carrying the same engine changes are the next step
